note: The main banks were taken as Serbia's three largest by assets, a choice from general knowledge (no central bank or association ranking was read in this pass): Banca Intesa, OTP banka Srbija and UniCredit Bank Srbija. Banca Intesa: its conditions of approval for the Visa Gold (enclosure 103, from 1 September 2023), Mastercard Gold (enclosure 93, from 1 January 2025) and Mastercard Platinum (enclosure 113, from 11 June 2026) credit cards, read 2026-10-30. Each bears a fixed nominal rate on spending in dinars, written (15.62%, 13.12% and 7.93% a year); the lower rates on spending in foreign currency (12.60%, 10.85%, 4.62%) aren't written. Their annual membership for the primary card is 6,000, 6,000 and 16,800 dinars; the Mastercard Gold's waiver and the Platinum's 25% or 30% reductions for holders of the bank's Magnifica or Hit Plus accounts aren't written, the game not holding those accounts. The monthly obligation is at least 5% of the total spent, at least 100 dinars (5 euros), plus interest and due fees. Cash at Banca Intesa's ATMs costs 3%, at least 90 dinars, on the Gold cards; the Platinum's sheet as read states none. Delay bears the statutory default rate where higher, which varies and isn't written. The Mastercard Standard is issued only within a payment account package, which the game doesn't hold, and isn't written. OTP banka Srbija's and UniCredit Bank Srbija's card terms weren't reached in this pass (UniCredit's sites elsewhere answered with an IP check). Wave 4 (30 October 2026): NLB Banka (the former NLB Komercijalna banka, one of the largest) and Addiko Bank were added because their card pages publish the terms at a plain address; OTP banka Srbija's and Raiffeisen's credit card addresses answered not found, and UniCredit Bank Srbija's card page was refused by its BrightCloud security filter, so none of them is written. NLB Banka's Visa credit card page, read 30 October 2026, gives representative examples (calculated 1 July 2025) for the Visa Revolving and Visa Revolving Gold: each a fixed nominal 12.00% a year, a monthly membership of 100 dinars (Gold 150) for a card outside an account package (nothing within the NLB IndiGo or Royal Blue packages, which the game doesn't hold, so it's charged in full), and a repayment model of 5% or 10% of the debt a month, the holder's choice, written as a 5% minimum. The credit bureau report (246 dinars) and promissory note (50 dinars) costs at signing aren't written. Its Mastercard Installment card (purchases split into instalments) and DinaCard cards, whose rate depends on the repayment model chosen, aren't written. Addiko Bank's Mastercard credit card page, read 30 October 2026, its representative example calculated 27 December 2024: a nominal 16.00% a year on revolving debt, the holder choosing the monthly repayment, at least 5% of the total debt, and no fee among the costs borne by the holder; no interest when the debt is repaid in full each month. Its instalment option's 2,400-dinar fee and the cash and foreign terms aren't stated there and aren't written.
